class="container"><message-content _ngcontent-ng-c3072953151="" _nghost-ng-c3457851425="" id="message-content-id-r_46ee5f19d63479cc" class="ng-star-inserted"><div _ngcontent-ng-c3457851425="" aria-busy="false" dir="ltr" style="--animation-duration: 600ms; --fade-animation-function: linear;"><p data-path-to-node="0">Yes, it is possible. Since you are already using <code data-path-to-node="0" data-index-in-node="49">Termux:Widget</code>, you are likely triggering scripts manually from your home screen. To expand this, you should shift from <b data-path-to-node="0" data-index-in-node="168">manual triggering</b> (push) to <b data-path-to-node="0" data-index-in-node="196">event-driven automation</b> (pull).</p><p data-path-to-node="1">In the Android/Termux environment, the primary bottleneck for automation is the <b data-path-to-node="1" data-index-in-node="80">Scoped Storage</b> model and <b data-path-to-node="1" data-index-in-node="105">Background Execution</b> restrictions.</p><h3 data-path-to-node="2">1. Event-Driven Automation with <code data-path-to-node="2" data-index-in-node="32">inotify-tools</code></h3><p data-path-to-node="3">Instead of clicking a widget to sort files, you can have a background script monitor your <code data-path-to-node="3" data-index-in-node="90">Downloads</code> or <code data-path-to-node="3" data-index-in-node="103">Documents</code> folder in real-time.</p><p data-path-to-node="4"><b data-path-to-node="4" data-index-in-node="0">Prerequisites:</b></p><ol start="1" data-path-to-node="5"><li><p data-path-to-node="5,0,0">Run <code data-path-to-node="5,0,0" data-index-in-node="4">termux-setup-storage</code> to ensure Termux can see <code data-path-to-node="5,0,0" data-index-in-node="50">/sdcard</code>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="5,1,0">Install the monitoring utility: <code data-path-to-node="5,1,0" data-index-in-node="32">pkg install inotify-tools</code>.</p></li></ol><p data-path-to-node="6"><b data-path-to-node="6" data-index-in-node="0">Logic:</b>
The following script monitors a directory for new files (<code data-path-to-node="6" data-index-in-node="64">create</code> or <code data-path-to-node="6" data-index-in-node="74">moved_to</code> events). When a file appears, it checks the extension and moves it to the defined client or document folder.</p><response-element class="" Integrating with <code data-path-to-node="14" data-index-in-node="20">Termux:Widget</code></h3><p data-path-to-node="15">You can keep using the widget to toggle these background "listeners" on or off.</p><ul data-path-to-node="16"><li><p data-path-to-node="16,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="16,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Start Script:</b> Creates a PID file and runs the <code data-path-to-node="16,0,0" data-index-in-node="46">inotify</code> script in the background using <code data-path-to-node="16,0,0" data-index-in-node="85">nohup</code>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="16,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="16,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Stop Script:</b> Reads the PID file and kills the process.</p></li></ul><h3 data-path-to-node="17">Technical Constraints &amp; Risks</h3><ul data-path-to-node="18"><li><p data-path-to-node="18,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="18,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Battery Optimization:</b> Androidâ€™s "Phantom Process Killer" or battery optimization will likely kill a long-running Termux process. You must go to <b data-path-to-node="18,0,0" data-index-in-node="144">App Info &gt; Battery</b> and set Termux to <b data-path-to-node="18,0,0" data-index-in-node="181">"Unrestricted"</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="18,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="18,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Atomic Moves:</b> When downloading files (like large PDFs), <code data-path-to-node="18,1,0" data-index-in-node="56">inotify</code> might trigger the <code data-path-to-node="18,1,0" data-index-in-node="82">CREATE</code> event before the file is fully written. It is safer to monitor for <code data-path-to-node="18,1,0" data-index-in-node="156">CLOSE_WRITE</code> to ensure the file is complete before moving it.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="18,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="18,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">AOSP Variance:</b> On newer Android versions (13+), background start restrictions are stricter. If the script fails to start from a widget, you may need to grant <code data-path-to-node="18,2,0" data-index-in-node="158">Allow background activity</code> explicitly in the system settings.</p></li></ul><p data-path-to-node="19">Would you like me to write a complete "Manager" script that handles starting/stopping these listeners for aria-busy="false" dir="ltr" style="--animation-duration: 600ms; --fade-animation-function: linear;"><p data-path-to-node="0">Your scripts reveal a sophisticated intake system that uses file hashes (SHA-256) to prevent duplicates and regex-based string manipulation to extract client names from filenames.</p><h3 data-path-to-node="1">System Audit &amp; Current Logic</h3><p data-path-to-node="2">The system currently operates with the following architecture:</p><ul data-path-to-node="3"><li><p data-path-to-node="3,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Deduplication:</b> Uses <code data-path-to-node="3,0,0" data-index-in-node="20">sha256sum</code> to ensure no identical file is processed twice.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Intake Routing:</b></p><ul data-path-to-node="3,1,1"><li><p data-path-to-node="3,1,1,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,1,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Images:</b> Scans <code data-path-to-node="3,1,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="14">Download</code> for non-system images and moves them to <code data-path-to-node="3,1,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="63">PRIVATE-IMAGES</code>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,1,1,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,1,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">PDFs:</b> Scans <code data-path-to-node="3,1,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="12">Download</code> for valid PDF headers. It attempts to extract a "Client" name using <code data-path-to-node="3,1,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="89">extract_client_folder()</code>.</p></li></ul></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Sanitization:</b> Replaces non-alphanumeric characters with underscores to prevent shell injection or filesystem errors.</p></li></ul><h3 data-path-to-node="4">The "Failed Transaction" Issue</h3><p data-path-to-node="5">The error <code data-path-to-node="5" data-index-in-node="10">cmd: Failure calling service package: Failed transaction</code> in your first screenshot is likely caused by the <code data-path-to-node="5" data-index-in-node="116">termux-api</code> package manager bridge being throttled or blocked by Android's <b data-path-to-node="5" data-index-in-node="190">Phantom Process Killer</b>.</p><p data-path-to-node="6"><b data-path-to-node="6" data-index-in-node="0">Fix:</b></p><ol start="1" data-path-to-node="7"><li><p data-path-to-node="7,0,0">Go to <b data-path-to-node="7,0,0" data-index-in-node="6">Android Settings &gt; Apps &gt; Termux</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="7,1,0">Set <b data-path-to-node="7,1,0" data-index-in-node="4">Battery</b> to <b data-path-to-node="7,1,0" data-index-in-node="15">Unrestricted</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="7,2,0">Ensure <b data-path-to-node="7,2,0" data-index-in-node="7">Allow background activity</b> is toggled ON.</p></li></ol><hr data-path-to-node="8"><h3 data-path-to-node="9">Expanding the Automation</h3><p data-path-to-node="10">Since you want to "add more," we can implement <b data-path-to-node="10" data-index-in-node="47">OCR (Optical Character Recognition)</b> and <b data-path-to-node="10" data-index-in-node="87">Auto-Categorization</b> based on document content rather than just the filename.</p><h4 data-path-to-node="11">1. Using <code data-path-to-node="22,0,0" data-index-in-node="152">close_write</code> in the watcher script prevents this.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="22,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="22,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Permission Scoping:</b> On Android 14+, <code data-path-to-node="22,1,0" data-index-in-node="36">~/.shortcuts</code> might require explicit <code data-path-to-node="22,1,0" data-index-in-node="72">MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE</code> permissions. Resolving the "Failed Transaction" Error</h3><p data-path-to-node="16">The <code data-path-to-node="16" data-index-in-node="4">cmd: Failure calling service package</code> error in your terminal means the Android system service is timing out when Termux tries to talk to it.</p><ul data-path-to-node="17"><li><p data-path-to-node="17,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="17,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">The Cause:</b> This is almost always the <b data-path-to-node="17,0,0" data-index-in-node="37">Android Phantom Process Killer</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="17,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="17,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">The Fix:</b> You need to disable the child process limit. Run this command in Termux:
<code data-path-to-node="17,1,0" data-index-in-node="82">/system/bin/device_config put activity_manager max_phantom_processes 2147483647</code>
<i data-path-to-node="17,1,0" data-index-in-node="162">(Note: This may require a one-time setup via ADB if you are on Android 12 or 13).</i></p></li></ul><p data-path-to-node="18"><b data-path-to-node="18" data-index-in-node="0">Would you like me to rewrite your PDF script into a single "Master Intake" script that handles both images and PDFs more efficiently?</b></p></div><!----></message-content><!----></div></structured-content-container><!----><!----><div _ngcontent-ng-c2576208498="" class="response-footer contains-extensions-response
